properties.description: A digest is a digest whichever dialect it arrives in (crates/reflow2-core/tests/checksum_dialect.rs) — 14 cases, 9 new for BL-160. PREFIX (BL-125): a bare hex digest matches its own `sha256:`-prefixed baseline and vice versa, the drift event id is identical whichever dialect was observed, and both counterweights hold — a genuinely different digest still reports `checksum_change` with its `realizes` edges intact, and a non-hex fingerprint is left verbatim. LENGTH (BL-160): a full 64-char digest matches a 16-char baseline and a truncated observation matches a full baseline, on the drift comparison AND on `set_artifact_checksum`'s would-move-the-baseline guard — the half that is not a gate problem at all but a BL-157 bulk sweep failing on every short-registered artifact for a change that never happened. When the two dialects agree the LONGER digest stays on the record, which also makes the accept idempotent ACROSS dialects: re-stating it coarsely mints one claim, not two. FIVE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and they are what keep the length rule from being a way to stop noticing: two FULL digests sharing their first sixteen characters are still drift (the case a truncate-both-to-N would pass); a truncated observation that disagrees WITHIN its own length is still drift; a genuinely different digest is still refused as a first baseline, still naming the disposition that would be honest; prefix tolerance does not escape the `sha256:` dialect, so `blake3:zz` and `blake3:zzzz` stay different; and an EMPTY digest agrees with nothing, because every string starts with the empty string. No minimum prefix length is imposed, deliberately — a short baseline is a weak baseline, but its strength is decided when it is REGISTERED, and a read side refusing to honour what the write side accepted is the same write/read disagreement this suite exists to close. `tools/reflow2_check.py`'s Python workaround is DELETED, and tools/test_reflow2_check.py pins the pair end to end: an untouched file registered short gates GREEN, and the same short baseline on a genuinely edited file still gates RED.
properties.findings: WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: the four bug cases failed and all five counterweights passed. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: make agreement always-true and all seven counterweights fail while every bug case passes (which is what proves the counterweights carry the weight); revert to `==` and exactly the four bug cases fail; drop the sha256-dialect restriction and only the two dialect-boundary cases fail; truncate both sides to 16 and only the two sharing-a-prefix cases fail; drop the both-non-empty guard and only the empty-digest case fails; fix drift.rs alone and only the two accept-path cases fail; drop the longer-digest-wins rule and only the idempotence case fails. THE TEST WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT: the first version of the still-refused counterweight used a SHORT baseline, and against a 16-char baseline `NEAR` is a legitimate extension rather than a different digest — a 16-char baseline only ever pinned 16 characters, which was established by writing it wrong rather than assumed. PROVEN ON THE REAL DESIGN, and it is the row's own scenario replayed: the built binary driven over stdio JSON-RPC against a throwaway copy of reflow2's own 1221-node design, sweeping all 109 registered artifacts off the actual working tree with the FULL 64-char digest — 51 truncated baselines, all 51 unchanged, and the only 4 `checksum_change` findings are the four files this change edited.
